subject: Tips for working with large datasets?

messages.author: 70d0917afd869432
messages.subject: Tips for working with large datasets?
parts:
Hi everyone!

I've recently been tasked with analyzing a very large dataset (N = ~150,000 cases, with 141 items).  The factor structure is also hypothetically complicated (with one of the hypothesized models being a four tier higher order model, but we are also going to try simpler models).  My issue is I only have the one PC to run the analyses on, with limited memory to do so (8 gigs of RAM).

I've tried running a few models so far, and had lavaan chug for a while and then crash with errors due to running out of memory.  I then tried to pare down the dataset (e.g., remove all cases with any missing data, only use cases from the USA), and the model (e.g., just with items loading on their respective factors with the CFA correlated LVs), but still ran into the same problem.

Does anyone have any advice on attempting such an analysis?  I've never worked with such a large dataset before, so any and all suggestions would be extremely welcome!

Thanks,

Matt

On 09/05/2014 02:15 AM, Matthew Sigal wrote:
> I've recently been tasked with analyzing a /very/ large dataset (N =

Do you have continuous data only? I would start with computing the
covariance matrix, and feed that to lavaan (using the sample.cov=
argument), instead of using the full dataset. Of course, this will not
allow you to deal with missing values and/or non-normal data, but you
will still be able to learn a lot.

If you have categorical data, try to update to the development version
(0.5-17), where we have made some changes in order to deal better with
large datasets.

Keep us posted.

Yves.
